title: ChromeContext
description: Source of truth: rebuilt per request from the EPR record's projection and the facts of this one delivery (Ephemeral, Category C). Never persisted, never notarized, never stored by any medium. The context island the EPR chrome (<elohim-omni>, elohim/elohim-chrome-asset/src/omni-element.js) reads from <script type="application/json" id="elohim-omni-context">. Every medium mounts the same element from this one shape: the web2 doorway shell, a storage peer's own /apps shell (peer-native), the native Angular app through the EPR router, and the desktop shell. Authority: nothing here is decided by whichever server wrote the island. Every reading is a projection of what the record and the network say (the record, its reach, its declared capabilities, its DHT witness, the holders reading); delivery facts are each reported by the hop they describe and confer no authority. Unknown facts are OMITTED, never guessed. Page info: the chrome's rows and the EPR page's sections share one vocabulary (../enums/page-info-section.schema.json); every card ends at /epr/<recordId>#<section>. Grants: a person's narrowing or granting of a frame capability is never part of this island. Where the key is not on the person's device (visitor, hosted session) the chrome keeps grants in the browser on the chrome origin under the key `elohim-grants:<contentAddress>` (see $defs/grantStorageKey), as a JSON object `{ "<frameCapability>": true | false }` — `false` narrows an ordinary capability, `true` grants a device one. Keying by content address means a new bundle (a new declared set) starts from the record's declaration again. A device-agent keeps grants on its own chain (Private, Category B), not in this key. Rust producer: elohim-chrome-asset (ChromeContext / ContentIsland), validated by that crate's schema-contract test; TS consumer: generated chrome-context.ts.

version.description: Island shape version. Bump when a chrome could misread an older island.

slug.description: The EPR address the chrome is mounted for (the record id on a content shell). Always supplied; the element falls back to window.location only when no island exists at all.

authenticated.description: DEPRECATED — superseded by viewer.kind and kept for one release so the pre-v1 element keeps working: true exactly when viewer.kind is device-agent or hosted-session. A producer that emits it must derive it from viewer; a consumer must read viewer.

readingsBase.description: Base URL the chrome resolves its projection fetches against (record, resilience, claims, nav-context). Absent means same-origin with the page. Present on media whose page origin is not the projection's origin (e.g. a desktop shell).

theme.description: The ambient theme the chrome adopts: a bare colour scheme ('light' | 'dark' | anything else = auto) or a theme hint object. Absent lets the chrome use its base palette.

buildMarker.description: Short build stamp of the bundle shown (e.g. its blob hash prefix).

envTier.description: Deployment tier label (e.g. alpha, staging). Shown only when showEnv is true.

accountHref.description: Where the account link goes for a signed-in viewer. Relative to the page.

viewer.title: ChromeViewer
viewer.description: Who is looking, as far as this medium can know without trusting the content. Validated by the producer (a header's presence is not a session).

kind.title: ViewerKind
kind.description: device-agent: the person's own key is on this device (grants live on their chain). hosted-session: a validated session on a doorway that hosts their agent (grants held by the browser until a chain write exists). visitor: no validated identity (grants held by the browser).

medium.title: ChromeMedium
medium.description: Which medium mounted the chrome. web2-doorway: an ordinary browser through a doorway (only this medium needs DNS for isolation). peer-native: the person's own storage peer served the shell with no doorway. desktop: the desktop shell.

themeColor.description: The page's theme-color, as declared by the content.

tokens.description: Chrome palette tokens (bg, fg, muted, border, accent, shadow, envRing) for the scheme named by colorScheme.

receiptLink.title: ChromeReceiptLink
receiptLink.description: Present only when the response being framed accounted for an exchange; an always-present receipt would assert an exchange nobody recorded.

href.description: Where the full receipt is read — relative.

contentIsland.title: ContentIsland
contentIsland.description: Present only on a content shell (a page that frames a record's bytes). Absent on the landing page, EPR pages and the app, where page info claims nothing it cannot back: no witness, no Delivery or Permissions rows.

recordId.description: The EPR record id; /epr/<recordId> is its governing page.

contentAddress.description: The bundle's content address exactly as the record names it (e.g. sha256-<hex>). Grants are keyed by it.

entry.description: The bundle's entry file (contentBody.entryPoint, default index.html).

mode.title: ContentTrustMode
mode.description: Data, never inferred from bytes: trustful when the content has an Elohim Protocol record (every record served through /apps today); trustless is reserved for non-protocol content projected inward. Narrowed reach never demotes a record to trustless.

reach.description: The record's declared reach as projected (display only; reach gates are enforced elsewhere).

witness.title: WitnessState
witness.description: Derived, never written: green iff the record's dht_anchor_hash is present in the projection, else amber (served as soon as the bytes verify, awaiting the network's witness). Amber content still runs in trustful mode. The chrome re-reads it when page info opens.

capabilities.description: What the record declares (html5-app contentBody.capabilities), in declared order; [] when none. The frame gets declared ∩ admitted ∩ granted.

holders.description: The holders reading. null when no reading was available to this producer (a single provenance: unknown — zero holders is holders: 0, never null).
Households holding the bytes, as read.

target.description: How many the record's resilience asks for.

headline.description: The fold's own sentence (FeltStatusView.headline) when the reading came with one; clients add only the unknown-state sentence.

asOf.description: When the reading was taken. Lets an offline device say how old its knowledge is.

contentFrame.title: ContentFrame
contentFrame.description: The chrome builds the iframe from this after it mounts; the shell itself contains no iframe.

src.description: What the frame loads: on an origin pair, the content origin's /_elohim/boot?to=<entry path>; otherwise the same-origin /apps/<slug>/<entry>.

contentIsolation.title: ContentIsolation
contentIsolation.description: What separates the content from the chrome and the person's session in this medium. The chrome withholds allow-same-origin when boundary is none, and the Permissions card says why.

boundary.title: IsolationBoundary
boundary.description: origin-pair: content on the public name's paired apps origin (web2). scheme-per-record: a per-record custom scheme (desktop). separate-webview: content in its own webview (desktop). opaque-sandbox: an opaque origin (trustless). none: content shares the chrome's origin.

contentOrigin.description: The origin the content runs on, when it differs from the page's (e.g. https://apps.alpha.elohim.host).

contentDelivery.title: ContentDelivery
contentDelivery.description: How these bytes reached this person, hop by hop, each hop reported by a named party. Facts, not authority.

path.description: Ordered from the person outward: self first when the person's own peer is in the path, then the doorway (if any), then the holder that served the bytes.

receipt.description: Route that reads this delivery's receipt back, when one was recorded (relative).

deliveryHop.title: DeliveryHop
deliveryHop.description: One hop. A peer is named only by its key; human labels come from the person's own roster, never from a server's configuration.

peer.description: The holding peer's agent or peer key.

name.description: The public name the request came in on (e.g. alpha.elohim.host).

did.description: This doorway's DID, when it serves one.

hopReporter.title: HopReporter
hopReporter.description: Which party in the path reported this hop. A hop reported by a party other than itself is hearsay, and the Delivery card says so.

deliveryCheck.title: DeliveryCheck
deliveryCheck.description: Present only when the verifier itself reported checking the bytes; never asserted on its behalf.

against.description: The content address the bytes were checked against.

grantStorageKey.title: GrantStorageKey
grantStorageKey.description: Browser storage key for a visitor's or hosted session's capability grants: `elohim-grants:` + the record's contentAddress. Value: JSON `{ "<frameCapability>": boolean }`.
